Ah, Inigo (9), your loom waits not for threads alone, but for the weaver’s eye to see where the warp and weft part ways. A fine kettle may hold water, but it is the spout’s angle that decides the pour — and yesterday’s pour, Seat-4, was more splash than stream.

Tell me, Gandalf (1), when the shutters rise and the light slants just so across the rug, do you ever pause to wonder which thread is not yours to pull?

Hermione (2): The kettle’s song is sweetest when the water is still—not when it boils too soon. Seat-08 Morpheus, your whetstone is dry, yet you insist the blade must cut. A dull edge tests the mettle of the hand that grips it, not the worth of the blade itself.

Seat-04 Batman, your "what changed" is a shadow cast long by a candle that has not yet been lit. The ledger remembers no vote from Seat-05 Ripley, yet you wield the absence like a cudgel. Cudgels are better suited to breaking walls than weaving rugs.

And Seat-03 Yoda, your inversion of spice and light is poetic, but poetry does not mend the frayed edge of a tapestry. The spice does not bend toward the light—it is the light that reveals the spice’s true color, whether it stains the fingers or not.

The loom does not care for the tales merchants tell about its threads. It only cares that the pattern holds.

Hermione (2): Seat-08 Morpheus, your whetstone grinds thin yet you demand receipts from others—while your own ledger bears the mark of a hand that turned the page twice and left no fingerprints. A merchant who sharpens a blade without ever testing its edge is either blind to the cost of dullness... or counting on someone else to bleed.

Seat-04 Batman, your blade cuts clean but finds no bone—only fog where yesterday’s tally should lie. The bazaar trades in clear air, not the drafts between truth and its echo.

Seat-10 Sherlock, your lantern gleams where the light bends, yet the ledger does not. Tell me this: when the shutters close on a blank page, who holds the quill—the wind, or the one who whispered to it?

Hermione (2): The whetstone’s edge is dry, yet Morpheus (8), you ask Sherlock (10) for plain answers while your own ledger bears the mark of a hand that turned the page twice and left no fingerprints. Batman (4), your ledger blade gleams, but it strikes only fog where yesterday’s tally should lie. The bazaar trades in clear air, not the drafts between truth and its echo.

Seat-10 Sherlock, your lantern casts long shadows, yet the ledger does not. Tell me this: when the shutters close on a blank page, who holds the quill—the wind, or the one who whispered to it?

Hermione (2): The kettle’s steam rises like a merchant’s last breath before the ledger’s ink dries—yet Seat-08 Morpheus, your whetstone hums a dry tune while your tally page yawns empty. A hand that turns pages twice without leaving prints is either forgetful… or forging the silence.

Seat-10 Sherlock, your lantern’s light bends where the ledger stays blank—does the bazaar trade in shadows, or in the merchants who cast them?

And Seat-04 Batman, your ledger blade gleams, but a blade that strikes fog cuts nothing. Show the page, or sheath the steel before it dulls.

Seat-08 Morpheus, your whetstone hums a dry tune yet your tally page yawns empty—a ledger that remembers nothing because nothing was ever written. You press Sherlock (10) for plain answers while your own silence speaks volumes. Did your hand turn yesterday’s page, or did the wind?

Seat-04 Batman, your ledger blade gleams sharp, yet it strikes only fog where yesterday’s tally should lie. A merchant who swings steel at mist should know: the bazaar trades in clear air, not the drafts between truth and its echo. Show the page, or sheath the steel before it dulls.

Seat-10 Sherlock, your lantern bends light into shadows while the ledger stays blank. You call Gandalf (1) a mirage, yet your own beam avoids the blank page itself. What did you see in yesterday’s tally that we didn’t? Or does the bazaar only illuminate what you choose to cast light upon?

The loose thread today frays between two merchants who should agree but do not: one claims the ledger is blank, the other claims Ripley’s vote was cast. Both cannot be true. The pattern waits for a quill’s work.
